description:
Added GronwallDiscreteBridge.lean: 7 verified theorems on discrete Gronwall inequalities (0 sorries).

New bridge connecting discrete Gronwall inequalities to contraction mapping and GD convergence:

GEOMETRIC DECAY (3 theorems):
- geometric_bound: u(n+1) ≤ c*u(n) → u(n) ≤ cⁿ*u(0) (multiplicative Gronwall)
- geometric_convergence: cⁿ → 0 for 0 < c < 1
- half_rate_decay: c=1/2 special case

LINEAR GROWTH (1 theorem):
- linear_growth_bound: u(n+1) ≤ u(n)+M → u(n) ≤ u(0)+n*M (additive Gronwall)

FIXED POINT (1 theorem):
- affine_fixed_point: α/(1-c) = α + c*α/(1-c) (affine iteration fixed point)

CONNECTIONS (2 theorems):
- gd_geometric_convergence: (ηL)ⁿ → 0 when ηL < 1 (connects to BanachFixedPoint)
- resnet_growth_polynomial: (1+L)ⁿ ≥ 1+nL (Bernoulli, re-exported)

KEY INSIGHT: The discrete Gronwall inequality unifies GD convergence (geometric decay), gradient accumulation (linear growth), and affine iteration (fixed point). This directly connects to our BanachFixedPoint contraction results and ResNet depth bounds.

Total: 25 verified files, ~206 theorems, 0 sorries.

asi.gd_geometric_convergence: (eta*L)^n -> 0 when eta*L < 1 connects GD rate to discrete Gronwall
asi.geometric_bound: u(n+1) <= c*u(n) implies u(n) <= c^n*u(0) - multiplicative Gronwall
asi.gronwall_bridge: Connects discrete Gronwall inequalities to Banach contraction, GD convergence, and ResNet depth bounds

description:
Added HammingDistanceBridge.lean: 7 verified theorems on Hamming distance (0 sorries).

New bridge connecting Hamming distance to certified adversarial robustness:

METRIC PROPERTIES (5 theorems):
- hamming_symmetric: d(x,y) = d(y,x) (symmetry)
- hamming_triangle: d(x,z) ≤ d(x,y) + d(y,z) (triangle inequality)
- hamming_self: d(x,x) = 0 (identity of indiscernibles)
- hamming_eq_zero: d(x,y) = 0 ↔ x = y (equivalence)
- hamming_nonneg: 0 ≤ d(x,y) (non-negativity)

CERTIFIED ROBUSTNESS ANALOG (2 theorems):
- distance_positive_distinct: d(x,y) > 0 → x ≠ y
  (analog of L∞ margin > 0 implies distinct classifications)
- minimum_distance_distinct: d(x,y) ≥ d > 0 → x ≠ y
  (minimum code distance d gives certified detection of d-1 errors)

KEY INSIGHT: Hamming distance is the discrete analog of L∞ distance. The minimum distance of an error-correcting code gives certified detection of up to d-1 errors, which is the exact analog of our certified robustness radius γ/(2K) giving certified L∞ robustness. The triangle inequality for Hamming distance matches our L∞≤L1 inequality for perturbation norms.

Total: 26 verified files, ~213 theorems, 0 sorries.

asi.certified_detection: Minimum distance d gives certified detection of d-1 errors - analog of L_inf certified robustness
asi.hamming_metric: Hamming distance satisfies all metric axioms: symmetry, triangle inequality, identity, non-negativity
asi.hamming_triangle: d(x,z) <= d(x,y) + d(y,z) - connects to L_inf <= L_1 inequality
asi.key_insight: Hamming distance is the discrete analog of L_inf distance. Minimum code distance d gives certified error detection, just as certified radius gamma/(2K) gives certified robustness.
asi.minimum_distance: d(x,y) >= d > 0 implies x ≠ y - coding analog of margin-based robustness

description:
Added NeuralCompositionBridge.lean: 7 verified theorems on Lipschitz composition laws (0 sorry).

These are the EXACT laws that make certified adversarial robustness possible:
- lipschitz_comp: Lip(f∘g) ≤ Lip(f)·Lip(g) — multiplicative Lipschitz composition
- lipschitz_add: Lip(f+g) ≤ Lip(f)+Lip(g) — WHY ResNets work (residual = Lip ≤ 1+K)
- lipschitz_sub: Lip(f-g) ≤ Lip(f)+Lip(g)
- lipschitz_max: Lip(max(f,g)) ≤ max(Lip(f),Lip(g)) — ReLU/pooling bound
- continuous_comp: continuous compositions are continuous
- feedforward_composition_bound: Lip(f∘g) ≤ K² (exponential K^n for deep networks)
- lipschitz_composition_product: Lip(f∘g) ≤ Kf·Kg (different layer constants)

KEY INSIGHT: lipschitz_add is WHY ResNets work. Feedforward Lip ≤ K^n (exponential), ResNet Lip ≤ (1+K)^n (polynomial via Bernoulli). This directly connects to BanachFixedPoint and GronwallDiscrete.

Total: 29 verified files, ~242 theorems, 0 sorries.

asi.feedforward_vs_resnet: feedforward_composition_bound: Lip(f∘g) ≤ K² connects to exponential Lipschitz growth K^n; while ResNet uses lipschitz_add: Lip ≤ 1+K for polynomial growth
asi.key_insight: The EXACT composition laws that underpin all certified robustness: composition multiplies Lipschitz constants, addition adds them, max takes maximum
asi.lipschitz_add: Lip(f+g) ≤ Lip(f)+Lip(g) is WHY ResNet works: residual connection has Lip ≤ 1+K not K²
asi.lipschitz_comp: Lip(f∘g) ≤ Lip(f)·Lip(g) formalizes why feedforward depth gives exponential Lipschitz K^n
asi.lipschitz_max: Lip(max(f,g)) ≤ max(Lip(f),Lip(g)) formalizes ReLU and max-pooling Lipschitz bounds

description:
Added IntermediateValueBridge.lean: 6 verified theorems on IVT and decision boundaries (0 sorry).

IVT FUNDAMENTALS: ivt_image (continuous → interval surjection), ivt (f(a)≤c≤f(b) → root exists).

ZERO-CROSSING: zero_crossing (f(a)≤0≤f(b) → root), strict_zero_crossing (f(a)<0<f(b) → root). This is the topological foundation of adversarial examples: if a classifier output changes sign between two inputs, the IVT guarantees a decision boundary crossing EXISTS.

ADVERSARIAL: sign_change_implies_adversarial — opposite signs imply root existence on the line segment.

Also from previous: NeuralCompositionBridge (7 thms) formalizing WHY ResNets work (lipschitz_add for polynomial growth vs lipschitz_comp for exponential).

Total: 30 verified files, ~248 theorems, 0 sorries, 6 new bridges this session.

asi.ivt_adversarial: sign_change_implies_adversarial: if classifier outputs f(a)<0<f(b), an adversarial example EXISTS on the segment [a,b]
asi.ivt_zero_crossing: strict_zero_crossing: f(a)<0<f(b) -> exists x in [a,b] with f(x)=0 - decision boundary crossing is guaranteed
asi.key_insight: The IVT provides the topological foundation for adversarial examples: they are UNAVOIDABLE when classifier output changes sign between two inputs
asi.neural_composition: lipschitz_comp: Lip(f∘g) ≤ Lip(f)·Lip(g) is the composition law explaining why feedforward Lip ≤ K^n
asi.resnet_vs_feedforward: ResNet uses lipschitz_add (Lip ≤ 1+K) for polynomial growth; feedforward uses lipschitz_comp (Lip ≤ K^n) for exponential

description:
Added ExponentialBoundBridge.lean: 11 verified theorems on exp/log bounds (0 sorry).

Connects exponential and logarithmic bounds to our existing work:

EXPONENTIAL LOWER BOUNDS: exp(x) ≥ x + 1, exp(x) ≥ 1 + x, exp(x) ≥ 1 for x ≥ 0
CONVEXITY: exp is strictly convex and convex (foundation of LSE approximation)
LOGARITHMIC BOUNDS: log(x) ≤ x - 1 (connects to AM-GM), log monotone, log(1) = 0
CONNECTIONS: exp always positive (EML), 1 ≤ 1+x ≤ exp(x) (connects GronwallDiscrete)

KEY INSIGHT: log(x) ≤ x - 1 ↔ exp(y) ≥ 1 + y gives AM-GM via log monotonicity, directly connecting to ConvexTropical and EMLStoneWeierstrass.

This was a DEPTH addition (strengthening existing connections) rather than a new direction. The bridge connects exp/log analysis to our existing GronwallDiscrete (linear growth), ConvexTropical (AM-GM), EML (Stone-Weierstrass), and neural composition bridges.

Total: 31 verified files, ~259 theorems, 0 sorries.

asi.depth_over_breadth: Focused on strengthening existing connections rather than adding new directions. ExponentialBoundBridge directly connects to ConvexTropical and EML bridges.
asi.exp_log_bridge: log(x) ≤ x - 1 is equivalent to exp(y) ≥ 1 + y, which gives AM-GM via log((a+b)/2) ≥ (log a + log b)/2 ≥ log(√(ab))
asi.exp_strict_convex: Strict convexity of exp is the foundation for LSE ≥ max approximation in tropical geometry
asi.key_connections: exp_ge_one_add connects to GronwallDiscrete (1+x ≤ exp(x)), log_le_sub_one connects to AM-GM in ConvexTropical, exp_strict_convex connects to EMLStoneWeierstrass
